newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Chemical sees lower yr net profit.
newsitem.headline: Australia Chemical sees lower yr net profit.

text.p: Australian Chemical Holdings Ltd said on Friday it expected a very substantial reduction in net profit for the year to September 30 compared with last year after a deterioration in trading conditions.

Australian Chemical Holdings, a chemical producer with operations in Australia and New Zealand, said there had been a significant downturn in trading conditions in the third quarter ending June 30 which was continuing in the fourth quarter.
"This trend, together with other operational factors, will make it difficult to add substantially to the profit earned in the first half," the company said.
"Therefore there will be a very substantial reduction in profit after tax for the full year ending September 30 1997 when compared with the profit achieved in the prior year," it said.
Australian Chemical reported a net profit of A$6.41 million for the year to September 1996 on sales of A$187.3 million, down from a net profit of A$9.69 million the previous year.
However, discussions between Australian Chemical's management and its major customers indicated an improvement in trading conditions in 1997/98.

A review of plant utilisation and strategy for future production has resulted in the board cancelling the proposed A$6 million expansion and upgrade at the Wacol, Queensland, plant in favour of a low cost replacement of existing plant, it said.
